images.title: HCF in three steps
images.purpose: Recap the common subparts method for the HCF in three short steps, using 28 and 42.
images.composition: Three numbered panels in one row joined by two grey arrows, each holding only a line or two, with generous space around.
exact_structure: Panel 1 (teal #0072B2 border), heading 1 Factorise: two lines 28 = 2 × 2 × 7 and 42 = 2 × 3 × 7.
Panel 2 (amber #E69F00 border), heading 2 Common subparts: the line 2, 7, 2 × 7.
Panel 3 (reddish purple #CC79A7 border), heading 3 Largest: the line HCF = 14.
Exactly 2 grey #6B7280 arrows: panel 1 to panel 2, panel 2 to panel 3.
rejection: any factorisation that does not multiply back to its number
images.takeaway: Factorise both numbers, find the subparts they share, and the largest shared subpart is the HCF.
images.description: Three panels: 28 and 42 factorised, common subparts 2, 7 and 2 × 7, and HCF = 14.
images.context: Shown beside the practice questions on common factors and the HCF.
images.teaching_notes: Follow the three panels in order for each practice pair; if step 2 is empty, the HCF is 1.

image_decisions.why: A three step recap supports the practice questions on the HCF.
